newsitem.title: UK: Qatar Airways introduce new inproved schedules.
newsitem.headline: Qatar Airways introduce new inproved schedules.

text.p: Privately owned Qatar Airways has announced a major restructuring plan to introduce new aircraft and new branding to take the airline forward into the next century.
Newly appointed chief executive Akbar Al Baker has brought in a number of airline executives to strengthen the management team.
The short-haul Boeing fleet is being refitted to enhance passenger comfort and a fourth aircraft will be added to improve schedules on routes to the Indian sub-continent.
New wide-body aircraft like Airbus A300 are being evaluated as replacements for the Boeing 747 fleet.

Services to London are being improved with the introduction of non-stop flights between Gatwick and Doha in early February. The airline has secured runway slots to transfer the Gatwick operation to Heathrow from mid May when the service will be increased to a daily frequency.

New schedules were recently introduced, including twice-daily direct services on intra-Gulf routes from Doha to Dubai and Abu Dhabi. There is an increase in frequency from Doha to Cairo and a new thrice-weekly service between Doha and Trivandrum from February 18.

"The aim of Qatar Airways is to become a world-class airlines, offering premium service at competitive prices. I am confident that, with the new management team and exciting development planned for our route network, we will achieve this aim," Akbar Al Baker said.
